findings.title: Exit code change from 4 to 3 for recreate-upgrade breaks documented contract and existing automation
findings.body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 in this PR. The public documentation in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc (lines 128-130) documents exit code 3 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration.' and exit code 4 as the new feature-disabled case. However, this is a breaking change to the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check` command: any existing CI/CD pipeline or script written against the previously released behavior (where exit code 4 meant 'recreate upgrade required') will now misinterpret exit code 4 as 'feature disabled' and exit code 3 as 'recreate upgrade'. Since the tool is explicitly documented as 'fully scriptable' and consumers 'should rely only on the exit code of the check command', silently renumbering an already-published exit code is an API/contract break. The recreate-upgrade code should keep its existing value (4) and the feature-disabled case should use a new, unused code (e.g., 5), or the change must be called out as a breaking change in release notes.

The `--features` CLI option is processed during configuration parsing/validation, which happens in validateConfig() (invoked via super.validateConfig() further down). This means Profile.isFeatureEnabled() reflects only the features from the persisted/optimized configuration or environment, not the `--features=rolling-updates` flag passed on the command line. Consequently, a user running `kc.sh update-compatibility check --file=... --features=rolling-updates` (exactly the invocation shown in docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc line 53 and used throughout UpdateCommandDistTest) would still get 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled.' and exit code 4, unless the feature was already enabled via KC_FEATURES environment variable or a prior build. The tests pass only because the distribution test harness may set the feature through the environment/build. The feature check must be moved after validateConfig() (or the profile must be re-evaluated with the parsed options) so that the documented `--features=rolling-updates` flag actually enables the command.

findings.title: CAUTION block claims the Operator will fail if rolling-updates is not enabled, which is inaccurate
findings.body: The new CAUTION block (lines 446-450) states: 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This is misleading: the operator does not fail when the feature is disabled. Per the rest of the same section (lines 461-466), when the feature is not enabled the operator simply falls back to the legacy Keycloak 26.1 behavior (scale down on image change). The feature flag gates the new update-strategy behavior (and the update-compatibility CLI commands), it does not cause the operator to fail. The wording should be corrected to say the update strategies require the feature to be enabled, not that the operator will fail.
